fixes.explanation: Yes, False is right, baker. The text says "People will live there, and never again will there be an utter destruction. So Jerusalem will dwell securely." (Zechariah 14:11). Just before that, the city "…will be raised up and will remain in her place…" (Zechariah 14:10). Never again is a big promise, and the city dwells securely. So no second round of utter destruction is coming.

Yes, that's it. "…the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar." (Zechariah 14:20). The everyday pots are put right alongside those bowls, and that's a big step up for a cooking pot. Then verse 21 says every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts.

Kings, huh? Crowns, capes, the whole parade, I like where your head's at, friend. But this verse lists no kings. It says "Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with Him." (Zechariah 14:5). The ones with Him are called the holy ones, and the text stops there. Even my mustache can't add names the verse doesn't give.

Priest is a fine job, friend, but the verse reaches for a bigger word. It says "On that day the LORD will become King over all the earth…" (Zechariah 14:9). A priest serves at an altar, but this verse is talking about the whole earth. Then it adds "…the LORD alone, and His name alone." (Zechariah 14:9).

Water jars by the well sound lovely, friend, and I'd have picked them too, mostly because I'm thirsty. But the text says the cooking pots "…will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar." (Zechariah 14:20). The comparison is to the bowls by the altar, not to anything out by the well. So those plain cooking pots get a big step up from the kitchen.

A storeroom is a sensible guess, the same way my old junk drawer was where things went to wait. But the verse says "…the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar." (Zechariah 14:20). These pots don't stay in storage. They're lined up with the bowls before the altar.
